response.sql:
WITH funding_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    p.fundflux,
    AVG(scanspatial.boxy / scanspatial.boxz) as avg_ratio,
    COUNT(DISTINCT p.arcregistry) as distinct_projects
  FROM scanspatial
  JOIN projects p ON scanspatial.arcref = p.arcregistry
  WHERE scanspatial.boxy IS NOT NULL 
    AND scanspatial.boxz IS NOT NULL
    AND scanspatial.boxz <> 0
  GROUP BY p.fundflux
),
avg_projects_count AS (
  SELECT AVG(distinct_projects) as cross_avg
  FROM funding_stats
),
filtered_sources AS (
  SELECT 
    fs.avg_ratio,
    fs.distinct_projects,
    apc.cross_avg
  FROM funding_stats fs
  CROSS JOIN avg_projects_count apc
  WHERE fs.distinct_projects > apc.cross_avg
)
SELECT 
  AVG(avg_ratio),
  SUM(distinct_projects),
  AVG(distinct_projects - cross_avg)
FROM filtered_sources

assumptions.assumption: Spatial records where boxz = 0 are excluded to prevent division by zero errors. Consequently, projects are counted in the distinct project count only if they have at least one spatial record where both boxy and boxz are non-NULL and boxz is non-zero.

alternatives.interpretation: Division by zero (when boxz = 0) should be treated as producing NULL rather than causing an error, allowing such records to contribute to the project count while being excluded from the average ratio. This preserves projects that possess spatial records with zero Z dimension.
